content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I previously raised this issue but haven’t received any feedback yet. Now I have a more precise question. According to the [product_name] manual, each Modbus connection can be set up as client or server, specifying local and remote IP addresses. The server acts as the data source and only responds when the client initiates a request. Does this mean that the data transfer table alone handles the requests, and the server won’t transmit data until the client requests it? Essentially, does the client determine when to receive information? Looking forward to your responses. Thank you.

Hello [user_name], The client-server model described here applies to the Modbus TCP standard and isn’t unique to [company_name] products. You can refer to sources from other automation providers for broader context, such as the guide from Prosoft Technologies related to Rockwell PLCs, which outlines the client-server relationship in Modbus TCP networks: [url]. Hope this clarifies the concept. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], I understand Modbus isn’t exclusive to [company_name] products. My main concern is whether those client requests in [product_name] are sent out automatically. Can the frequency of these requests be adjusted? Appreciate your help, [user_name]!

Hello [user_name], I’m not a specialist in [product_name], but I have worked with various controllers using Modbus TCP. From my experience, client requests aren’t sent out automatically; you usually have to set the parameters within the controller’s configuration. There’s an example on the Product Support portal where [product_name] runs as a Modbus TCP client for acquiring measurement data via Modbus TCP/IP: [url]. Hope this information helps. Regards, [user_name]
Perhaps this information will be useful.
Understood, [user_name]. So that interval determines how often the client initiates requests, according to the settings you choose. Thank you. Making the most of quarantine with [company_name].
Hello [user_name], If you don’t set this option, the [product_name] applies an automatic interval, although I’m not sure what the default value is.
During my search, I found a tutorial about connecting ESP32-MODBUS RTU RS485 with PLC STEP-7 200 (Read/Write): [url]. This helped me read and write data via Modbus. Hope it’s helpful for you.
However, [product_name] isn’t equivalent to S7-200 smart and can’t use Modbus RTU. [product_name] supports only Modbus TCP/IP for Modbus communication.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are asking for detailed guidance on Modbus TCP client-server behavior in [company_name] [product_name] environments, specifically questioning whether client requests are automated or require explicit programming. There’s a general lack of clarity about whether [product_name] can automatically generate requests and about how communication intervals are configured. Users are also mixing up supported Modbus protocols for different [company_name] controllers, suggesting documentation gaps regarding Modbus features and protocol compatibility across controller models.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are hoping for simple, documented options in [product_name] to configure and manage the automation and timing of Modbus TCP client requests. Clear documentation of automatic behaviors and direct settings for request intervals are expected.
